# BuildPulse MCP Server

> Model Context Protocol server for BuildPulse. BuildPulse provides faster, cheaper CI runners for GitHub Actions, CircleCI and Semaphore (about 2x faster at half the cost, 3,000 free minutes a month, no card) with Test Intelligence built in: flaky-test detection, coverage and CI metrics. Twelve read-only tools: runner usage, cost and savings versus GitHub list price, configured runner labels, runner activation status, plus flaky tests, recent CI failures, per-run test results, flakiness % and code-coverage % for a repository. Callable from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, and any MCP-aware agent.

The server is hosted at `https://mcp.buildpulse.io/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) and published to npm as `@buildpulse/mcp` (stdio). Both transports expose the same twelve tools, five prompts, and two resource templates. An organization that has not activated runners can be pointed at `https://buildpulse.io/organizations/{orgId}/runners/setup`. Authentication is a BuildPulse API token (`bp_<64-hex>`; legacy 40-hex tokens also work) sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration for hosted clients. Every tool is read-only and scoped to the organizations the token can access.

## Connect

- [Hosted endpoint](https://mcp.buildpulse.io/mcp): Streamable HTTP. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http buildpulse https://mcp.buildpulse.io/mcp`. Claude.ai and ChatGPT connectors: paste the URL.
- [OAuth discovery](https://mcp.buildpulse.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server): RFC 8414 metadata; dynamic client registration at /oauth/register.
- [npm: @buildpulse/mcp](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@buildpulse/mcp): local stdio transport. Run `npx -y @buildpulse/mcp` with `BUILDPULSE_TOKEN` set.
- [MCP Registry: io.github.BuildPulseLLC/buildpulse-mcp](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=buildpulse): official registry listing.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/BuildPulseLLC/buildpulse-mcp): Go, MIT licensed.

## Tools

- get_runner_status: whether the organization has activated BuildPulse runners, its billing mode, and when it has not, a `how_to_start` sentence (3,000 free minutes a month) with the setup URL.
- get_runner_usage: runner jobs, billable minutes, cost before and after free minutes, p50/p90 job duration, queue wait, and the same minutes at GitHub list price with the savings percentage, per size and provider; `days` 1-90, default 30. The `pricing` block carries the rate card.
- get_runner_configs: the runner sizes and `runs-on` labels (or CircleCI resource class / Semaphore agent type) the organization has configured.
- list_my_organizations: every organization the token can access; returns the `id` UUID used as `organization_id` on org- and repo-scoped calls.
- list_repositories: repositories BuildPulse monitors for an organization.
- find_flaky_tests: a repository's flaky-test inventory over the last 14 days, sorted by disruptiveness or recency.
- get_test_history: recent disruption events for one test, with build URL and commit SHA.
- list_recent_submissions: the most recent CI runs that uploaded results for a repository.
- get_submission_test_results: per-test results for one CI run; filter to failures.
- get_recent_failures: every test that failed across the last N CI runs, aggregated by test identity.
- get_repo_flakiness: current flakiness % for a repository (last 14 days).
- get_repo_coverage: current code-coverage % from the latest report.

Multi-tenant rule: if `list_my_organizations` returns two or more organizations, pass `organization_id` on every repo-scoped call. The server does not guess; omitting it returns an error that lists the accessible organizations and their UUIDs.

## Prompts

- estimate_runner_savings: runner status first; with no tenant, estimate CI minutes from recent runs and price them at BuildPulse versus GitHub list rate (prices from the API), then the setup URL; with a tenant, the last 30 days of usage and savings.
- triage_flaky_tests: rank a repository's flaky tests and propose next steps.
- ci_health_check: flakiness + coverage snapshot for a repository.
- explain_test_failure: walk through one test's recent failures.
- whats_red: what broke CI on the most recent runs.

## Documentation

- [MCP install hub](https://platform.buildpulse.io/docs/mcp): per-client setup for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, and ChatGPT.
- [Platform API llms.txt](https://platform.buildpulse.io/llms.txt): the REST API these tools call.
- [Platform API OpenAPI](https://platform.buildpulse.io/openapi.yaml): machine-readable API contract.
- [Security and threat model](https://github.com/BuildPulseLLC/buildpulse-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md): read-only surface, tenant isolation, rate limits, audit log.

## BuildPulse

- [BuildPulse](https://buildpulse.io): CI runners for GitHub Actions, CircleCI and Semaphore with Test Intelligence included: flaky-test detection, quarantine, code coverage, engineering metrics.
- [Runners](https://buildpulse.io/products/runners): 2x faster, half the cost, 3,000 free minutes a month; benchmarks published.
- [Products](https://buildpulse.io/products): what BuildPulse ships.
- [Pricing](https://buildpulse.io/pricing): runner rates and Test Intelligence plans; API and MCP access come with a paid Test Intelligence plan or a paid runner subscription.
- [Support](mailto:support@buildpulse.io): support@buildpulse.io.
